title: Dispense ten counted tablets from a counting tray into a vial
instruction: Put exactly the ten counted tablets from the counting tray's trough into the vial, keeping the vial off the table while they go in. The six other tablets stay on the tray's counting area, and no tablet may be spilt.
context: Counting tablets on a counting tray and pouring the count into a vial is a core pharmacy-technician task. The counted tablets wait in the tray's trough, the rest stay on its counting area, and the vial is kept off the counter as they go in so none bounce out. A robot that dispenses medicines must get the count exactly right: one tablet too many, too few or dropped spoils the prescription.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A loose blue ABS-plastic counting tray, 60 g, 9 x 8 cm with rims 1.5 cm tall, centred 31.5 cm forward and 4 cm left of the centre line. Along its right side runs a trough 2 cm wide behind a divider 8 mm high; the trough opens at the back into a chute 3.5 cm long. Left of the divider is the counting area, a flat floor 8.4 x 5.1 cm closed by rims on its other three sides. A grip fin 1.2 cm thick stands on the front rim and reaches 5 cm forward, 1.2 to 4.8 cm above the tray's underside. (2) 16 loose white film-coated tablets, all alike: discs 8 mm across and 3.5 mm thick, 0.3 g each. The 10 counted ones lie in two rows of five near the front of the trough, the 6 others in two rows of three on the counting area. (3) An empty square amber polypropylene vial, 5 x 5 cm and 4.5 cm tall, 20 g, standing 17.8 cm forward and 6.5 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged on the tablets' positions throughout the trial. In the vial: a tablet's centre inside the vial, up to 4 mm above its rim. On the tray: its centre over the tray's floor or chute and at most 2 cm above the tray's underside; on the counting area: on the tray, left of the divider. Spilt: a tablet outside the vial and the tray with its centre at most 1 cm above the table, or on the floor. Held up: the vial's underside at least 2 cm off the table each time a tablet goes in. Only the 10 counted tablets, those that started in the trough, earn credit. 0.0 for the whole trial (latched, never reset) if any of the 6 others is ever in the vial or any tablet is ever spilt; also 0.0 if at the end a tablet is neither in the vial nor on the tray, or fewer than all 6 others are on the counting area. Otherwise: 1.0: all 10 counted tablets in the vial, held up as each went in; 0.5: 5 to 9 of them in the vial, or all 10 but not all held up; 0.25: 1 to 4 in the vial; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s. In a real trial the tablets look alike, so the referee counts and reads the three videos: at the end, exactly 10 in the vial, exactly 6 on the counting area, and none in the trough or chute, on the table or the floor; at no time a tablet on the table or the floor, or one entering the counting area; and the vial's underside at least 2 cm up as each tablet drops in. This pins down which tablets moved: the 6 started apart on the counting area and the 10 in the trough, and a tablet could reach the counting area only over the divider or a rim, which the videos would show. So the 6 still there are the 6 others, and the tablets in the vial are counted ones. The same counts give the partial tiers.
reset_notes: Put the ten counted tablets back in two rows near the front of the trough and the six others in two rows on the counting area, lay the tray where it was and stand the empty vial in its place.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the tablets are 16 rigid discs (8 mm across, 0.3 g), slick like film-coated tablets (friction 0.15); the tray and the vial are rigid, and the vial is a square open box. The simulation knows which tablet is which; a real trial tells them apart by counts and video (see scoring). Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
